problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}=\frac{2x+B}{{x}^{2}+5}-\frac{1}{x+1},
$$

where $B$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x.$

feedback.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}=\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{D}{x+2},
$$

where $D$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $D.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+4x+3 & =2x(x+2)+D({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=-2$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-2)^{2}+4(-2)+3 & =2(-2)(-2+2)+D((-2)^{2}+3) \\ 7 & =7D \\ D & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+3=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+3| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3)+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+C\end{aligned}
$$
